transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, I guess what brought me in is... I keep hearing this man’s voice. It comes right out of the garage vents at the shop, and sometimes even from under the hood of the cars I'm working on. It’s as clear as somebody standing right next to me, and he keeps telling me not to trust my husband, and warning me not to touch certain cars. Which is a real problem because I have to do the diagnostics. 

Like the other day, we had this '14 Subaru come in, completely rusted out on the exhaust. The guy tried to tell me he just bought it from a dealer up in Syracuse. Upstate New York salt is just brutal on the undercarriage, you know? I drove through there once for a weekend trip back when I was taking some classes at the community college, and the roads were just awful. I was studying business back then, thinking I'd open my own shop eventually, maybe specialize in imports, but... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, why I'm here. Yeah, so that guy's voice under the hood just won't stop talking to me about my husband.
Have you been needing much less sleep than usual and still feeling full of energy?

Yeah, actually. For weeks at a time, I’ll sleep maybe two, maybe three hours max. I just wake up way before dawn, and my mind is already in the garage, running through all the repairs. I just feel like sleeping more would be a complete waste of time. 

Time is money, right? And there's always so much to organize at the shop. Like the tool chests. I swear, the 10-millimeter sockets just grow legs and walk away. Every mechanic will tell you that. You buy a brand new set, and three days later, the 10-mil is just gone. I think they fall down into the engine bay and bounce out on the highway. I actually saw a whole ratchet sitting on the shoulder of I-95 once when I was driving down to see my sister. She lives down in Richmond now. Nice house, but the plumbing is terrible. She had this leak in the guest bathroom that completely ruined the drywall on the ceiling below it, and the contractor charged her an absolute fortune to patch it up. I told her she should have just watched a YouTube video and done it herself, it's really just mud and tape, you know? But... wait. Sorry. What were we talking about? Oh, right, sleep. But yeah, two or three hours is plenty, I have tons of energy.
Have you ever heard that voice during a time when your mood and energy felt normal?

Yeah, actually. Even when things calm down... like, there was this stretch of a few weeks where I was actually sleeping normally, maybe seven or eight hours, and I wasn't rushing around trying to reorganize the entire shop or making all these huge plans. But that voice in the garage? Still there. Still coming out of the vents. And I still knew, without a doubt, that my husband and my boss were tracking me. 

Tracking devices are getting so small now, you wouldn't believe it. I was reading this article on my phone while I was waiting in line at the DMV—which, by the way, is an absolute nightmare. I had to renew my registration, and they had exactly two people working the counter for a room of like fifty people. One guy was arguing about a title transfer for a boat. Who even buys a boat in this economy? Unless you live on a lake, it's just a hole in the water you throw money into. My uncle had a pontoon boat once, and the motor kept flooding. We spent more time fixing the carburetor than actually fishing. Fishing is supposed to be relaxing, but not when you're smelling like gasoline all afternoon. But anyway... um, where was I? Oh, the tracking. Yeah, even when I was feeling totally normal and sleeping fine, I still heard the voice and knew they were watching me.
Have you used methamphetamine, cocaine, or other drugs around the times when you hear the voice?

No, no, I don't touch any of that stuff. Never have. I mean, you can't be high and work around heavy machinery, it's just asking to lose a finger. Or worse. 

I actually saw a guy lose a finger once, well, part of one. It was back when I was working at this quick-lube place right out of high school. He got his hand caught in the serpentine belt of an old Chevy Tahoe because he wasn't paying attention. Blood everywhere. And the manager, oh man, he was more worried about the paperwork than the guy's hand. That manager was a real piece of work. He used to drive this totally tricked-out Honda Civic, lowered suspension, loud exhaust, the whole nine yards. But he drove it like a grandma because he was terrified of scratching the rims on a pothole. Potholes around here are basically craters, though. The city never fixes them right, they just throw some cold patch in there and call it a day, and the first time it rains, it all washes right out. It's terrible for your suspension. I replace so many ball joints and tie rod ends just because of this city's roads. If they just did it right the first time... 

Wait, what was the question? Oh, drugs. Right. No, no drugs at all. Just coffee. Lots of coffee.
Have you had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

No, not really. I mean, I don't think I've ever just sat around feeling down like that for weeks on end. There's just too much to do, you know? Even when I'm tired, I still have to get up and go to the shop. 

The shop gets so incredibly hot in the summer, especially around August. We have these big bay doors, but they don't really let a breeze in, they just let the sun bake the concrete. Last year, my boss bought us these massive industrial fans, the ones that sound like an airplane taking off. But all they really do is push the hot air around. It's like standing inside a convection oven. I told him we should just invest in one of those swamp coolers, but he's so cheap. He won't even buy the good hand cleaner, the one with the pumice in it. We have this cheap orange stuff that smells like artificial citrus and leaves your hands feeling greasy. I actually started buying my own and keeping it in my locker. My locker is a disaster right now, though. I have like three different winter coats stuffed in there because the weather here can't make up its mind. One day it's freezing, the next day you're sweating through your coveralls... 

Um... sorry, what were we talking about? Depression? Right, no. I haven't really had anything like that.
For how long have you been hearing that man’s voice?

Well, the voice and knowing about the tracking... that's been going on for about ten months now. Yeah, ten months. Because it started right around the time I was trying to fix up this old '68 Mustang fastback. 

Beautiful car, honestly. The guy who owned it wanted it painted this specific shade of cherry red, but he brought in the cheapest aftermarket parts you've ever seen. I kept telling him, you can't put a cheap fiberglass hood on a classic like that, it's never going to line up right with the fenders. The gaps will look terrible. But people watch these car shows on TV and think you can restore a vehicle in a weekend with a socket set and some zip ties. It takes hundreds of hours of bodywork just to get the panels straight before you even think about primer. And sanding... oh my god, the sanding. You'll be blowing dust out of your nose for a week. I actually prefer mechanical work over bodywork anyway. Rebuilding a transmission is like a puzzle, you know? Everything has a specific place. You miss one snap ring, and the whole thing tears itself apart as soon as you put it in drive. My dad taught me how to rebuild a carburetor when I was twelve. We did it on the kitchen table, and my mom was so mad because we spilled solvent on her good tablecloth. It had these little embroidered daisies on it... 

Wait, sorry. Ten months. Yeah, it's been about ten months since all this started.
During that ten-month period, was there ever a stretch of at least two weeks when you were hearing the voice or felt tracked while your mood and energy were otherwise normal?

Yeah, definitely. Actually, there was a stretch... maybe a month or two ago? Things were pretty quiet. I wasn't staying up all night or making all those big plans to open my own custom shop. I was actually sleeping a lot more, just feeling kind of normal, energy-wise. But the voice in the garage was still there, clear as day. And I still knew my husband and my boss were tracking me. 

My husband actually bought me this new phone right around then, which just proved it. He said it was because my old one had a cracked screen, but I know it's because the new ones have better GPS chips. The screen on my old one wasn't even that bad, honestly. It just had this one spiderweb crack in the bottom corner from when I dropped it on a transmission jack. Those jacks are incredibly heavy, by the way. If you don't pump them up evenly, the whole tranny can slide right off, and you're looking at a crushed foot. We had a guy at the shop, a lube tech, who almost dropped a whole transfer case on himself because he wasn't paying attention. He was always on his phone, texting his girlfriend. She used to bring him lunch sometimes, these really good homemade tamales. Pork with green chile. I haven't had a good tamale since this little food truck down by the rail yard closed up. They had the best salsa verde, it was so spicy it would make your ears ring, but you couldn't stop eating it. I tried making it at home once, but I couldn't get the tomatillos to roast right. They just got mushy and stuck to the pan...

Wait, sorry. Yes. Even when my energy was totally normal and I was sleeping fine, the voice and the tracking stuff never stopped.
Did the voice first start soon after you had any serious medical problem, head injury, or seizure?

No, nothing like that. I haven't had any seizures or big medical issues. I mean, I bump my head on the lift arms at the shop sometimes, but just normal bumps. Those lift arms are solid steel, though. You learn pretty quick to wear a bump cap if you're working under a low clearance. We had this one guy, Gary, who refused to wear one, and he stood right up into the oil drain plug of an F-250. Cut his scalp wide open. Scalp wounds bleed like crazy, you know? It looked like a horror movie in bay three. We had to use like three bags of that industrial absorbent floor sweep just to clean it up. 

That floor sweep is basically just glorified kitty litter, honestly. I don't know why the shop suppliers charge so much for it. I buy the cheap stuff for my cat, Barnaby, but he kicks it absolutely everywhere. I had to get him one of those enclosed boxes with the little plastic flap door, but he just sits in there and bats the door back and forth for hours. It makes this clicking sound that drives me crazy when I'm trying to watch TV. He's a good cat, though. Found him behind a dumpster at the tire shop. He was just a tiny little thing, covered in grease...

Um, wait. Head injuries? Right. No, no serious head injuries or anything for me. I've always been pretty healthy.
During that time when your sleep and energy felt normal, did the voice continue for at least one full month?

I'm not exactly sure if it was a whole month. It's hard to keep track of time like that, you know? Time just sort of blends together, especially when you're working flat rate at the shop. You're just trying to beat the book time on every job so you can actually make a decent paycheck. Like, the book might say replacing a heater core takes eight hours, which is a joke because on some of these newer SUVs, you have to pull the entire dashboard out. The whole steering column, the airbags, the center console—everything has to come out just to get to this one little plastic box against the firewall. 

I actually had a customer yell at me once because his car was in the shop for three days for a heater core. He kept saying, "It's just a little radiator, how hard can it be?" People have no idea. They think cars are still built like they were in the seventies, where you could actually fit your hand between the engine block and the radiator fan. Now everything is packed in so tight you need specialized, low-profile ratchets just to change a spark plug. I spent a hundred and fifty bucks off the tool truck last week just for this one flex-head wrench. The tool truck guys are basically loan sharks, I swear. They pull up every Tuesday, hand you a complimentary donut, and suddenly you're in debt for the next five years because you just had to have the new impact gun with the fancy green casing...

But yeah, I don't know if the quiet period lasted a full month. It was just a while.
At any point, did the voice continue for a full month while your mood and energy felt normal?

Well, like I said, it was definitely a few weeks. It was a quieter time, you know? I was actually sleeping a lot more, and I wasn't staying up making all those huge plans for my custom shop. I felt pretty normal, energy-wise. But even then, I still heard the voice out in the garage, and I still knew for a fact that my husband and my boss were tracking me. 

Speaking of my boss, he actually brought in donuts the other day. Glazed ones from that place over on 4th Street. They’re good, but they always leave that sticky glaze all over your fingers, which is the last thing you want when you’re about to grab a torque wrench. If your hands are sticky, all the grease and brake dust just clings to you. I usually use this heavy-duty pumice soap we have in the washroom, the kind that feels like you're scrubbing your hands with actual sand. It takes off everything, even that black RTV silicone sealant. That silicone is a nightmare if you get it on your clothes. I ruined a perfectly good pair of Dickies work pants last month because I brushed up against a water pump I had just sealed. The pants were practically new, too. I had just bought them because my old ones were getting holes in the knees from kneeling on the concrete all day. You'd think they'd make a decent knee pad for mechanics, but the ones they sell always slide down around your ankles the second you start walking. I saw this guy on YouTube who actually cut up an old yoga mat and glued it inside his pants... 

Wait, what were you asking? Oh, right. Yeah, even during those quieter weeks when I was sleeping fine, the voice and the tracking stuff never went away.
Was there ever a period of at least two weeks when you were hearing the voice while not feeling especially up or energized?

Yeah, definitely. Like I was just saying, there was that quieter time, a few weeks there, where I was sleeping a lot more. I wasn't feeling all revved up or staying awake all night making those huge plans for my custom shop. I felt pretty normal, not energized at all. But even then, during those quiet weeks, I still heard the voice out in the garage. And I still knew they were tracking me—my husband and my boss. 

It's weird how they think they can hide it, honestly. Like my boss, he thinks he's so slick, but I know how the shop's Wi-Fi network is set up. We have this router in the back office, right? And it's one of those commercial ones with the big antennas. The guy from the internet company came out to install it, and he had this huge spool of CAT6 cable. He was complaining the whole time because he had to run it through the drop ceiling, and the ceiling tiles in the shop are covered in this thick layer of black dust from the exhaust fumes. Whenever you move a tile, it just rains black soot everywhere. I had to wipe down my entire toolbox afterward. My toolbox is a Snap-on, cherry red. Cost me more than my first car, but it's worth it because the drawers have those soft-close glides. If you slam a drawer full of heavy sockets in a cheap box, the whole thing rattles and eventually the tracks bend. I saw a guy drop a whole drawer of half-inch drive impact sockets on his foot once because the track gave out. Broke three toes. He had to wear this special boot for a month, and he couldn't even press the clutch pedal on his own car... 

But yeah, anyway, even when I wasn't feeling up or energized for those couple of weeks, the voice and the tracking were definitely still there.
Before you first started hearing the voice ten months ago, had you ever had a period like this where you needed much less sleep and felt unusually energized?

Yeah, actually. The whole thing with the long stretches of getting barely any sleep, having all these racing plans for the shop, and just nonstop activity... that all started about eleven months ago. So, yeah, a little before the voice showed up. 

I remember because that was right around the time I decided I was going to completely rebuild the transmission on this '98 Silverado we had sitting in the back lot. I was up for like three days straight just tearing into it. Transmissions are a totally different beast, you know? A lot of mechanics won't even touch the internals. They just swap the whole unit out and call it a day. But I was so wired, I just started pulling out all the clutch packs and the valve body right there on the bench. 

Have you ever smelled burnt automatic transmission fluid? It is literally the worst smell on earth. It’s this sharp, metallic, rotten fish smell that just gets into your pores. You can take three showers and you still smell like burnt ATF. My husband actually made me sleep on the couch that week because of the smell. Well, that and because I was pacing around the living room at 3 AM drawing up blueprints for the transmission dyno I was going to build from scratch. I even went out and bought all this steel tubing to weld the frame for it. Welding is tricky though, especially TIG welding. You need a really steady hand, and you have to get the argon gas flow just perfect or the weld gets all porous and weak. I watched this guy on TV build a whole sand rail frame in like two days, but they edit out all the prep work. The prep work is like ninety percent of welding. You have to grind off all the mill scale and clean the joints with acetone, otherwise the puddle just pops and spits at you. I ruined a really good pair of gloves because a piece of slag popped right through the leather...

Wait, sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, right, the energy. Yeah, the super energized, no-sleep stuff definitely started around eleven months ago.
After the high-energy, little-sleep period ended, did the voice keep going for at least one month?

Yeah, exactly. I think I mentioned that earlier, right? There was that quieter time, a few weeks, where I was sleeping a lot more. I wasn't making all those huge plans for the custom shop or feeling wired. But even then, I still heard the voice out in the garage, and I still knew for a fact that my husband and boss were tracking me. 

It's just crazy how they go about it. Like my husband, he's always on his phone, acting like he's just playing games or whatever, but I know he's checking the location app. He's got this old iPhone, the screen is completely shattered in the corner. I told him he should just get one of those DIY screen replacement kits online. I replaced the screen on my phone last year. It's actually not that hard if you have the right tools, but the screws are tiny. Like, microscopic. You have to use this special little pentalobe screwdriver, and if you sneeze, you lose half the screws on the carpet. I had to use a magnet to find one I dropped. Magnets are a lifesaver in the shop, too. We have these long magnetic pickup tools for when you drop a socket down into the engine bay. Because there is nothing worse than dropping a 10-millimeter socket. It's like they just disappear into another dimension. You can shine a flashlight down there for an hour and never find it. I swear there's a black hole at the bottom of every engine bay just for 10-millimeter sockets. I must have bought fifty of them in my career... 

But yeah, anyway, the voice and the tracking were still happening even when I was sleeping fine and not feeling all energized.
Was there ever a full month when you were hearing the voice while not feeling especially up or energized?

A full month? Um, I don't know if it was a whole month. I'd have to look at a calendar. Calendars are getting so expensive now, have you noticed that? The ones with the nice glossy pictures of classic cars, they want like twenty bucks for them at the auto parts store. I usually just wait until February when they put them on clearance for two dollars. Though last year I got this really cool one that had vintage muscle cars, and January was a '69 Chevelle SS. Beautiful car. My uncle had one when I was a kid, painted hugger orange with the black racing stripes down the hood. He used to take me for rides on Sundays and let me shift the gears from the passenger seat. It had a Hurst shifter with this big white cue ball knob. I always wanted to put a cue ball shifter in my truck, but it's an automatic, so it just wouldn't look right. You know, some people try to fake it, they put a boot over the automatic shifter to make it look like a manual, but anyone who knows anything about cars can spot that from a mile away. It's like putting an M-badge on a regular BMW 328i. You're not fooling anybody, you're just making yourself look silly... 

But yeah, I don't know if it was a full month. I really couldn't say for sure.
At any time since this started, did the voice continue for a full month when you were not feeling especially up or energized?

Well, like I was saying before, I know there was that quieter stretch. It was a few weeks where I was sleeping a lot more, you know? I wasn't wired, I wasn't drawing up all those huge plans for the shop or anything. But even then, during those quieter weeks, I still heard the voice out in the garage, and I absolutely still knew my husband and boss were tracking me. 

It's just exhausting, honestly. Being tracked like that. It drains the battery on your phone so fast, too. Location services are the number one battery killer on smartphones. I actually bought this heavy-duty portable power bank to keep in my toolbox because my phone kept dying by like 2 PM. It's one of those rugged ones, encased in rubber so if you drop it on the concrete floor of the shop, it doesn't shatter. Concrete is unforgiving. I dropped a brand new torque wrench on the floor once and it completely threw off the calibration. You have to send them out to get recalibrated, and it takes weeks. You can't just guess with torque specs, especially on things like cylinder head bolts. If you over-torque them, you stretch the bolts and ruin the threads in the block. If you under-torque them, you blow a head gasket. It's a very precise science. People think mechanics just hit everything with an impact gun until it's tight, but that's how you snap bolts. I had an apprentice once who sheared off three lug studs on a customer's minivan because he didn't know how to set the torque stick on his air gun...

But, yeah, to answer your question, even when I wasn't feeling all energized and up, the voice and the tracking were still happening during those quieter weeks. I just don't know if it added up to exactly a full month.
Looking back over these ten months, was there ever a full month when you were hearing the voice while your mood felt normal?

I feel like a broken record here, doc. I really don't know if it added up to exactly a full thirty days. But like I've been saying, there was definitely a quieter few weeks where my mood was pretty level, I was sleeping a lot more, and I wasn't making all those huge plans for the shop. But even then, during that quiet stretch, I still heard the voice out in the garage and I still believed 100 percent that my husband and boss were tracking me. 

Sleeping more was nice, honestly, except my mattress is starting to sag right in the middle. It's like sleeping in a ditch. I keep seeing those ads for the memory foam ones that they ship to you rolled up in a cardboard box. It's crazy how they compress them down that small. They must use some kind of massive industrial vacuum pump to suck all the air out. We have a pneumatic vacuum bleeder at the shop for doing brake jobs, and that thing pulls some serious negative pressure. You just hook it up to the bleeder valve and it sucks all the old fluid and air bubbles right out of the lines. Brake fluid is nasty stuff, though. It's highly corrosive. If you spill it on a car's paint, it'll eat right through the clear coat and base coat in like ten minutes. You have to wash it off immediately with soapy water. I had a guy come in once who tried to top off his own master cylinder and spilled half the bottle down the fender of his brand new F-150... 

But yeah, I don't know about a full month, just those quieter weeks.
Have the voice and the feeling of being tracked been present, in total, for at least six months?

Yeah, definitely. It's been about ten months now that all this has been going on. Ten whole months of dealing with the voices and knowing they're tracking me. It feels like it's been a lot longer, to be honest. Ten months is a long time to be on edge. That's almost a whole year. You know, we have a lot of cars that come into the shop that haven't had an oil change in ten months, or even a year, and the oil comes out looking like black sludge. People just ignore the sticker on their windshield. They think synthetic oil means they can just drive forever without changing it. But the filter still gets clogged, you know? The paper element inside the filter gets saturated with carbon and metal shavings, and then the bypass valve opens, and you're just circulating dirty oil right back through the engine bearings. That's how you spin a rod bearing. I had this lady bring in a Hyundai Sonata last week, and the engine was knocking so loud it sounded like someone was hitting the oil pan with a hammer. She said, "Oh, I just had the oil changed." I pulled the dipstick, and it was bone dry. People lie to their mechanics all the time, just like they probably lie to doctors. They think we can't tell... 

But yeah, it's been about ten months since this all started.
Thinking about the ten months this has been happening, was there ever a time when the voice was still there for a whole month while your mood felt completely normal?

Doc, are you even listening to me? We're just going in circles now. I honestly can't give you an exact thirty-day calendar count. Like I keep telling you, yes, there was a quieter stretch of a few weeks. My mood was fine, I was sleeping a lot more, and I wasn't drawing up those massive plans for the shop. But the voice in the garage was absolutely still there, and I still knew for a fact my husband and my boss were tracking my every move. 

You keep asking for this exact, precise timeframe, and it's driving me a little crazy. It reminds me of customers who come in with a check engine light and expect an exact answer in two seconds. They think you just plug in the OBD-II scanner under the dash and a little screen says, "replace the oxygen sensor." But the scanner just gives you a code, like a P0171, system too lean. It doesn't tell you the exact part that failed. You still have to do the actual diagnostic work. It could be a vacuum leak, it could be a clogged fuel injector, it could be a bad mass airflow sensor. I spent three hours last Tuesday smoke-testing the intake on a Chevy Cruze trying to find a leak. Those 1.4-liter Ecotec engines are notorious for PCV issues. The valve is literally built right into the plastic valve cover, which is just the stupidest design ever because the plastic warps from the engine heat over time, and then you have to replace the entire cover instead of a two-dollar valve. GM really dropped the ball on that engineering, I swear they just want to force people to buy more expensive parts...

But anyway, I can't give you a precise reading on if it was exactly a month. Just that there were those quiet weeks where I was sleeping and not energized, but the tracking and the voice never stopped.
During the last ten months, what is the longest stretch of time you heard the voice while your mood felt completely normal?

I mean, I don't know the exact number of days, doc. I keep saying, the longest stretch was just... a few weeks. It was a quieter few weeks. My mood was completely normal, I was sleeping a lot more, and I wasn't, you know, making all those huge plans for the shop. But even then, I still heard the voice out in the garage, and I still fully believed my husband and boss were tracking me. 

Speaking of the shop, we just got this new alignment rack installed last month, and it is a beast. It's a Hunter Hawkeye Elite, and the cameras on that thing are so precise, it's unbelievable. You just clamp the targets onto the wheels—they don't even touch the rim, they grab the tire tread so you don't scratch up people's nice alloy wheels. I hate when guys use the old style clamps and gouge the clear coat. Anyway, you roll the car forward a few inches to compensate the sensors, and boom, all your camber, caster, and toe readings are right there on the screen in like ninety seconds. It saves so much time compared to the old string-and-tape-measure method we used to have to do on lowered cars. We get a lot of kids bringing in these stanced out Honda Civics with like negative eight degrees of camber, just chewing through tires every three thousand miles. I try to tell them, "Look, your contact patch is the size of a credit card, you're going to hydroplane if you hit a puddle," but they don't listen. They just care about how it looks for Instagram... 

But yeah, the longest stretch was just those few weeks where my mood was level but the voice and the tracking were still happening.
What is the longest time the voice kept going when your mood felt completely normal?

Look, doc, I don't know how many different ways I can say the exact same thing. Are you writing this down? Because I feel like I'm repeating myself. Like I said, it was a few weeks. That was the longest stretch. A quieter few weeks where I was actually sleeping more, my mood was normal, and I wasn't, you know, staying up all night making those huge expansion plans for the shop. 

But even then, during those few weeks, I still heard the voice out in the garage. And I still knew, absolutely knew, that my husband and my boss were tracking me. 

It's like when a customer brings their car back three times for the same noise, and every time I tell them it's the wheel bearing, but they don't want to pay for the hub assembly, so they keep asking if it's just a rock stuck in the brake dust shield. I had this guy with a Ford F-150 do that last month. He swore up and down it was just a rock. I put it on the lift, grabbed the tire at 12 and 6 o'clock, and shook it—the whole wheel had like an inch of play in it. I told him, "Buddy, your wheel is about to fall off on the highway." But he didn't want to hear it because a new hub on a 4x4 F-150 is a few hundred bucks just in parts. People just hear what they want to hear, you know? They think if they ask the question enough times, the answer will magically change to something cheaper or easier. 

But my answer isn't changing. It was a few weeks where I felt normal, but the voice and the tracking never stopped. I really don't know how else to explain it to you.

I drove through there once for a weekend trip back when I was taking some classes at the community college, and the roads were just awful. I was studying business back then, thinking I'd open my own shop eventually, maybe specialize in imports, but... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, why I'm here. target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the duration of psychotic symptoms (hearing voices) in the absence of a mood episode (not feeling up or energized), which corresponds to the requirement of delusions and hallucinations occurring for 2 or more weeks without a major mood episode.

patient.answer:
Well, like I was saying before, I know there was that quieter stretch. It was a few weeks where I was sleeping a lot more, you know? I wasn't wired, I wasn't drawing up all those huge plans for the shop or anything. But even then, during those quieter weeks, I still heard the voice out in the garage, and I absolutely still knew my husband and boss were tracking me. 

It's just exhausting, honestly. Being tracked like that. It drains the battery on your phone so fast, too. Location services are the number one battery killer on smartphones. I actually bought this heavy-duty portable power bank to keep in my toolbox because my phone kept dying by like 2 PM. It's one of those rugged ones, encased in rubber so if you drop it on the concrete floor of the shop, it doesn't shatter. Concrete is unforgiving. I dropped a brand new torque wrench on the floor once and it completely threw off the calibration. You have to send them out to get recalibrated, and it takes weeks. You can't just guess with torque specs, especially on things like cylinder head bolts. If you over-torque them, you stretch the bolts and ruin the threads in the block. If you under-torque them, you blow a head gasket. It's a very precise science. People think mechanics just hit everything with an impact gun until it's tight, but that's how you snap bolts. I had an apprentice once who sheared off three lug studs on a customer's minivan because he didn't know how to set the torque stick on his air gun...

But, yeah, to answer your question, even when I wasn't feeling all energized and up, the voice and the tracking were still happening during those quieter weeks. I just don't know if it added up to exactly a full month.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic symptoms have persisted for at least one month outside of mood episodes, which is the key remaining discriminator between schizoaffective disorder and bipolar I disorder with psychotic features.
doctor.question: Looking back over these ten months, was there ever a full month when you were hearing the voice while your mood felt normal?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 3
target_item.manifestation: Even during a quieter few weeks when I was sleeping more and wasn’t making huge plans, I still heard the garage voice and believed my husband and boss were tracking me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the hallucinations (hearing the voice) occurred for a significant period (a month) while my mood was normal (absence of a major mood episode). This maps directly to Additional Requirement 3.

patient.answer:
I feel like a broken record here, doc. I really don't know if it added up to exactly a full thirty days. But like I've been saying, there was definitely a quieter few weeks where my mood was pretty level, I was sleeping a lot more, and I wasn't making all those huge plans for the shop. But even then, during that quiet stretch, I still heard the voice out in the garage and I still believed 100 percent that my husband and boss were tracking me. 

Sleeping more was nice, honestly, except my mattress is starting to sag right in the middle. It's like sleeping in a ditch. I keep seeing those ads for the memory foam ones that they ship to you rolled up in a cardboard box. It's crazy how they compress them down that small. They must use some kind of massive industrial vacuum pump to suck all the air out. We have a pneumatic vacuum bleeder at the shop for doing brake jobs, and that thing pulls some serious negative pressure. You just hook it up to the bleeder valve and it sucks all the old fluid and air bubbles right out of the lines. Brake fluid is nasty stuff, though. It's highly corrosive. If you spill it on a car's paint, it'll eat right through the clear coat and base coat in like ten minutes. You have to wash it off immediately with soapy water. I had a guy come in once who tried to top off his own master cylinder and spilled half the bottle down the fender of his brand new F-150... 

But yeah, I don't know about a full month, just those quieter weeks.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic symptoms have persisted for at least 6 months overall to distinguish schizophrenia from schizophreniform/brief psychotic disorder and support a primary psychotic disorder over mood disorder with psychotic features.
doctor.question: Have the voice and the feeling of being tracked been present, in total, for at least six months?

target_item.name: Psychotic Symptoms Duration
target_item.manifestation: The voices and tracking beliefs have been happening for about ten months now.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the psychotic symptoms (voice and feeling tracked) have been present for at least six months, which directly matches the psychotic symptoms duration in the profile.

patient.answer:
Yeah, definitely. It's been about ten months now that all this has been going on. Ten whole months of dealing with the voices and knowing they're tracking me. It feels like it's been a lot longer, to be honest. Ten months is a long time to be on edge. That's almost a whole year. You know, we have a lot of cars that come into the shop that haven't had an oil change in ten months, or even a year, and the oil comes out looking like black sludge. People just ignore the sticker on their windshield. They think synthetic oil means they can just drive forever without changing it. But the filter still gets clogged, you know? The paper element inside the filter gets saturated with carbon and metal shavings, and then the bypass valve opens, and you're just circulating dirty oil right back through the engine bearings. That's how you spin a rod bearing. I had this lady bring in a Hyundai Sonata last week, and the engine was knocking so loud it sounded like someone was hitting the oil pan with a hammer. She said, "Oh, I just had the oil changed." I pulled the dipstick, and it was bone dry. People lie to their mechanics all the time, just like they probably lie to doctors. They think we can't tell... 

But yeah, it's been about ten months since this all started.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there have been clear psychotic symptoms in the absence of mood symptoms for at least one month, which best distinguishes schizoaffective disorder from bipolar disorder with psychotic features.
doctor.question: Thinking about the ten months this has been happening, was there ever a time when the voice was still there for a whole month while your mood felt completely normal?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 3
target_item.manifestation: Even during a quieter few weeks when I was sleeping more and wasn’t making huge plans, I still heard the garage voice and believed my husband and boss were tracking me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is again asking if the psychotic symptoms (the voice) occurred during a period of normal mood, which corresponds to the requirement of psychotic symptoms occurring for 2 or more weeks in the absence of a major mood episode.

patient.answer:
Doc, are you even listening to me? We're just going in circles now. I honestly can't give you an exact thirty-day calendar count. Like I keep telling you, yes, there was a quieter stretch of a few weeks. My mood was fine, I was sleeping a lot more, and I wasn't drawing up those massive plans for the shop. But the voice in the garage was absolutely still there, and I still knew for a fact my husband and my boss were tracking my every move. 

You keep asking for this exact, precise timeframe, and it's driving me a little crazy. It reminds me of customers who come in with a check engine light and expect an exact answer in two seconds. They think you just plug in the OBD-II scanner under the dash and a little screen says, "replace the oxygen sensor." But the scanner just gives you a code, like a P0171, system too lean. It doesn't tell you the exact part that failed. You still have to do the actual diagnostic work. It could be a vacuum leak, it could be a clogged fuel injector, it could be a bad mass airflow sensor. I spent three hours last Tuesday smoke-testing the intake on a Chevy Cruze trying to find a leak. Those 1.4-liter Ecotec engines are notorious for PCV issues. The valve is literally built right into the plastic valve cover, which is just the stupidest design ever because the plastic warps from the engine heat over time, and then you have to replace the entire cover instead of a two-dollar valve. GM really dropped the ball on that engineering, I swear they just want to force people to buy more expensive parts...

But anyway, I can't give you a precise reading on if it was exactly a month. Just that there were those quiet weeks where I was sleeping and not energized, but the tracking and the voice never stopped.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic symptoms have occurred outside of mood episodes long enough to support schizoaffective disorder rather than bipolar disorder with psychotic features.
doctor.question: During the last ten months, what is the longest stretch of time you heard the voice while your mood felt completely normal?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 3
target_item.manifestation: Even during a quieter few weeks when I was sleeping more and wasn’t making huge plans, I still heard the garage voice and believed my husband and boss were tracking me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking for the exact duration of the psychotic symptoms occurring without mood symptoms, which corresponds to the requirement of delusions and hallucinations occurring for 2 or more weeks in the absence of a major mood episode.

patient.answer:
I mean, I don't know the exact number of days, doc. I keep saying, the longest stretch was just... a few weeks. It was a quieter few weeks. My mood was completely normal, I was sleeping a lot more, and I wasn't, you know, making all those huge plans for the shop. But even then, I still heard the voice out in the garage, and I still fully believed my husband and boss were tracking me. 

Speaking of the shop, we just got this new alignment rack installed last month, and it is a beast. It's a Hunter Hawkeye Elite, and the cameras on that thing are so precise, it's unbelievable. You just clamp the targets onto the wheels—they don't even touch the rim, they grab the tire tread so you don't scratch up people's nice alloy wheels. I hate when guys use the old style clamps and gouge the clear coat. Anyway, you roll the car forward a few inches to compensate the sensors, and boom, all your camber, caster, and toe readings are right there on the screen in like ninety seconds. It saves so much time compared to the old string-and-tape-measure method we used to have to do on lowered cars. We get a lot of kids bringing in these stanced out Honda Civics with like negative eight degrees of camber, just chewing through tires every three thousand miles. I try to tell them, "Look, your contact patch is the size of a credit card, you're going to hydroplane if you hit a puddle," but they don't listen. They just care about how it looks for Instagram... 

But yeah, the longest stretch was just those few weeks where my mood was level but the voice and the tracking were still happening.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are persistent psychotic symptoms outside mood episodes for at least one month, to distinguish schizoaffective disorder from bipolar disorder with psychotic features.
doctor.question: What is the longest time the voice kept going when your mood felt completely normal?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the duration of the hallucinations (the voice) occurring in the absence of a mood episode (when mood felt completely normal), which corresponds to the requirement of psychotic symptoms lasting for 2 or more weeks without a major mood episode.

patient.answer:
Look, doc, I don't know how many different ways I can say the exact same thing. Are you writing this down? Because I feel like I'm repeating myself. Like I said, it was a few weeks. That was the longest stretch. A quieter few weeks where I was actually sleeping more, my mood was normal, and I wasn't, you know, staying up all night making those huge expansion plans for the shop. 

But even then, during those few weeks, I still heard the voice out in the garage. And I still knew, absolutely knew, that my husband and my boss were tracking me. 

It's like when a customer brings their car back three times for the same noise, and every time I tell them it's the wheel bearing, but they don't want to pay for the hub assembly, so they keep asking if it's just a rock stuck in the brake dust shield. I had this guy with a Ford F-150 do that last month. He swore up and down it was just a rock. I put it on the lift, grabbed the tire at 12 and 6 o'clock, and shook it—the whole wheel had like an inch of play in it. I told him, "Buddy, your wheel is about to fall off on the highway." But he didn't want to hear it because a new hub on a 4x4 F-150 is a few hundred bucks just in parts. People just hear what they want to hear, you know? They think if they ask the question enough times, the answer will magically change to something cheaper or easier. 

But my answer isn't changing. It was a few weeks where I felt normal, but the voice and the tracking never stopped. I really don't know how else to explain it to you.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has clear manic symptoms (weeks of needing only 2–3 hours of sleep, high energy, racing/planning behavior, nonstop activity, grandiose business/engineering plans, pressured/tangential speech) together with persistent psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations and persecutory delusions). Psychosis was present for about 10 months overall and also persisted during a period of at least a few weeks when mood and energy were reported as normal, arguing against psychotic symptoms occurring only during mania. There is no sustained major depressive episode, no substance trigger, and no medical/neurologic cause identified. Schizophrenia was considered, but the history includes a prominent manic syndrome. Bipolar I disorder with psychotic symptoms was considered, but the interview did not establish a full month of psychosis outside mood episodes, so schizoaffective remains the best fit among the provided options.
